lessons.summary: How to choose between one well-structured deployable and many independent services, using four criteria (team topology, deploy independence, data ownership, operational cost), how to spot a distributed monolith, and how to migrate in either direction safely.

lessons.title: Service boundaries and domain-driven decomposition
lessons.summary: How to decide where one service (or module) ends and the next begins — using bounded contexts, invariants and change patterns — how each service owns its data, and how to spot the chatty boundary that tells you a line was drawn in the wrong place.

lessons.title: API gateway and Backend for Frontend
lessons.summary: One front door for many services (API gateway) and one tailored back end per client type (Backend for Frontend) — what each solves, what to put in each, how to aggregate calls without making failures worse, and when a plain reverse proxy is enough.

lessons.title: CQRS in production
lessons.summary: Running separate write and read models for real — the levels of CQRS from query classes to asynchronous projections, how to build idempotent checkpointed projections, how to measure and live with lag (including read-your-writes), how to rebuild read models safely, and when an index, a view or a replica is the better answer.

lessons.title: Event sourcing in production
lessons.summary: Storing every change as an immutable event and deriving state from them — the PostgreSQL event store schema and its concurrency and ordering traps, snapshots, event versioning with upcasters, deleting personal data from immutable history with crypto-shredding, rebuilding projections without re-running side effects, and when an audit table is all you need.

lessons.title: Saga orchestration and choreography
lessons.summary: Run long business processes across services in production with a process manager, durable timers, compensation retries and parking, end-to-end tracing and the metrics that tell you a saga is stuck before a customer does.

lessons.title: Strangler fig migration and anti-corruption layer
lessons.summary: Replace a legacy system one feature at a time behind a routing facade, protect the new model from the old one with an anti-corruption layer, and keep data in sync in both directions until each piece is safely cut over.

lessons.title: Change data capture
lessons.summary: Turn every committed database change into an ordered stream of events by reading the database's own log, with PostgreSQL logical replication or Debezium, and run it safely in production through slot monitoring, idempotent consumers and careful schema changes.

lessons.title: Multi-tenancy
lessons.summary: Serve many customer organisations from one platform by choosing silo, pool or bridge isolation per tier, resolving the tenant on every request, enforcing isolation in PostgreSQL with row-level security, and keeping one noisy tenant from hurting the rest.

lessons.title: Multi-region, active-active and active-passive
lessons.summary: Run one system in two or more geographic regions without lying to yourself about what it costs. Choose between active-passive and active-active, keep each tenant's data inside the country that requires it, resolve conflicting writes deliberately, and rehearse failover until it is boring.

lessons.title: Search architecture
lessons.summary: How a search engine finds "bridge tenders in Patna" among millions of documents in milliseconds. Build a tiny inverted index with BM25 ranking in C#, learn how OpenSearch/Elasticsearch clusters split and copy that index, keep it in sync with PostgreSQL through an outbox or CDC, and know when PostgreSQL full-text search is all you need.

lessons.title: Workflow engines and feature flags
lessons.summary: Long-running business processes must survive crashes, deploys and week-long waits. Learn how durable execution engines (Temporal, Azure Durable Functions, Elsa) persist and replay workflow state, when a hand-rolled state table is enough, and how feature flags with deterministic percentage rollouts and kill switches let you release that code safely.

lessons.title: Cloud design patterns catalogue
lessons.summary: Eighteen proven patterns for building on the cloud, each with the problem it solves, how it works, when to use it and when not to. Build the valet key, lease-based leader election, claim check, queue-based load levelling with competing consumers, throttling and health endpoints in ASP.NET Core.

lessons.title: Multi-level caching and rate limiting at scale
lessons.summary: Combine a tiny, very fast in-process cache (L1) with a shared distributed cache (L2), keep them consistent with pub/sub invalidation and short TTLs, and use .NET's HybridCache well. Then scale rate limiting beyond one server with distributed counters, sliding windows and local token leases that keep Redis traffic low.

lessons.title: Cost-aware architecture and architecture evolution
lessons.summary: Architecture is not a drawing you finish; it is a set of decisions you keep revisiting as load, team and budget change. Learn to size for the next 10x rather than an imaginary 1000x, to encode the properties you care about as automated fitness functions, to record decisions as ADRs that can be superseded, and to plan migrations as roadmaps with gates instead of big-bang rewrites.

modules.title: Real-World HLD Case Studies
modules.description: Twenty complete system design walkthroughs.

lessons.title: URL shortener
lessons.summary: Design a service that turns long links into short ones and redirects billions of clicks quickly, covering ID generation with base62, redirect semantics, read-heavy caching, click analytics and abuse control.

lessons.title: Pastebin
lessons.summary: Design a service for sharing text snippets by link, covering metadata versus content storage, unguessable keys, expiry and burn-after-read, safe rendering of user content, and how cleanup jobs and lifecycle rules keep storage from growing forever.

lessons.title: File storage service (Drive-style)
lessons.summary: Design a Drive-style file storage and sync service, covering content chunking and hashing, deduplication and garbage collection, a metadata store with a per-namespace change journal, multi-device sync and conflicts, and folder sharing with inherited permissions.

lessons.title: Notification platform
lessons.summary: Design a multi-channel notification platform (push, SMS, email, WhatsApp, in-app) with user preferences and quiet hours, versioned localised templates, frequency caps and provider rate limits, retries with backoff and dead-lettering, and priority lanes that keep OTPs fast during a marketing blast.

lessons.title: Chat application (WhatsApp-style)
lessons.summary: Design a WhatsApp-style messenger end to end — persistent connections, per-conversation ordering, sent/delivered/read receipts, offline delivery, groups and an overview of end-to-end encryption — with capacity maths, a PostgreSQL data model and C# for the sequencing core.

lessons.title: Social media news feed
lessons.summary: Design a social news feed — fan-out on write versus fan-out on read, the hybrid that solves the celebrity problem, time-sortable ids, k-way feed merging and a simple ranking pipeline — with capacity maths, PostgreSQL and Redis data models, and C# for the merge and ranking core.

lessons.title: Video streaming platform (YouTube-style)
lessons.summary: Design a YouTube-style video platform — resumable uploads, a parallel transcoding pipeline, HLS/DASH adaptive bitrate streaming, CDN delivery at terabits per second, and view counting that survives millions of events per second — with capacity maths, a PostgreSQL data model and C# for the ladder, playlist and counter core.

lessons.title: Ride-hailing platform (Uber-style)
lessons.summary: Design an Uber-style ride-hailing backend — high-rate driver location updates, geospatial indexing with geohash, H3 or quadtrees, driver matching with exclusive offers, surge pricing and a guarded trip state machine — with capacity maths, a PostgreSQL data model and C# for geohash encoding and the trip lifecycle.

lessons.title: Food delivery platform
lessons.summary: Design a food delivery backend — menus and ordering, restaurant acceptance with timeouts, delivery-partner dispatch that times arrival to food readiness, order batching, live tracking and ETA — with capacity maths, a PostgreSQL data model and C# for the order lifecycle, dispatch scoring and ETA.

lessons.title: E-commerce platform (Amazon-style)
lessons.summary: Design an Amazon-style e-commerce backend — catalog and search, carts, a checkout saga with inventory reservations that expire, payments, the order pipeline and flash sales for a hot SKU — with capacity maths, a PostgreSQL data model and C# for reservations, checkout and a flash-sale admission gate.

lessons.title: Movie ticket booking system
lessons.summary: Design a BookMyShow-style movie ticket system — seat maps, all-or-nothing seat holds with a TTL, payment timeouts and late payments, and a waiting room for blockbuster releases — with capacity maths, a PostgreSQL data model that makes double booking impossible, and C# for seat holds and the booking flow.

lessons.title: Hotel reservation system
lessons.summary: Design a hotel central reservation system — a per-night availability calendar, all-or-nothing multi-night bookings, a deliberate overbooking policy, and synchronising inventory with online travel agencies without selling the same last room twice — with capacity maths, a PostgreSQL data model and C# for the calendar, overbooking and channel sync.

lessons.title: Payment processing system
lessons.summary: Design a payment processing system for an online marketplace — a double-entry ledger with a balance invariant, idempotent payment APIs, integration with external payment service providers, signed webhooks that arrive late and out of order, daily reconciliation against settlement files, and a PCI scope kept as small as possible.

lessons.title: Search autocomplete service
lessons.summary: Design search autocomplete (typeahead) for a large e-commerce site — a trie with precomputed top-k suggestions at every node, offline aggregation of search logs into ranked phrases, immutable snapshots swapped without downtime, prefix caching in the browser and CDN, trending updates and light personalisation, all within a keystroke-sized latency budget.

lessons.title: Distributed rate limiter
lessons.summary: Design a distributed rate limiter for a public API platform — token buckets and sliding windows kept atomic in Redis with Lua scripts, a local-plus-global layering that keeps the hot path fast, rule configuration with tiers and shadow mode, correct 429 responses, and an explicit fail-open versus fail-closed policy for when the limiter itself breaks.

lessons.title: Logging and analytics platform
lessons.summary: Design a central logging and product-analytics platform — agents and an ingestion gateway with backpressure, Kafka as the durable buffer, stream processing for parsing, redaction, rollups and alerts, batch jobs for heavy aggregation and backfills, columnar OLAP storage with hot, warm and cold tiers, and sampling and retention policies that keep a 50 TB-per-day firehose affordable.

lessons.title: Real-time collaborative editor
lessons.summary: Design a Google-Docs-style collaborative editor — operational transformation versus CRDTs (with a tiny RGA CRDT in C#), per-document session servers with fenced leases, presence, an op log plus snapshots for persistence, and the capacity maths behind it.

lessons.title: Online examination platform
lessons.summary: Design an online exam platform for a million candidates starting at the same second — pre-staged encrypted papers, a server-authoritative timer, idempotent answer autosave, proctoring event pipelines and result publication — with capacity maths, a grading SQL exercise and C# for the integrity core.

lessons.title: Learning management system
lessons.summary: Design a multi-tenant learning management system for hundreds of institutions — tenant resolution and isolation, enrolment and seat licences, signed video delivery through a CDN, progress tracking that coalesces heartbeats, assessments and certificates — with capacity maths, a progress-report SQL exercise and C# for the tenancy and progress core.

lessons.title: Multi-tenant enterprise project management system
lessons.summary: Design a SaaS platform where hundreds of organisations manage infrastructure projects — roads, metro lines, water schemes — with strict isolation, role-and-attribute permissions, versioned documents, multi-step approvals, cross-project reporting, a tamper-evident audit trail and per-tenant data residency.

modules.title: Real-World LLD Case Studies
modules.description: Twenty object-oriented design problems, fully implemented.

lessons.title: Parking lot
lessons.summary: Design a multi-level car park with spot sizes, tickets and hourly pricing, and make sure two cars can never be given the same spot, even when they arrive at the same millisecond.

lessons.title: Elevator control system
lessons.summary: Design the control software for a bank of lifts in an office tower, with a LOOK scheduling algorithm per car, a pluggable dispatcher that picks which car answers a hall call, and a thread-safe controller driven by a clock tick.

lessons.title: ATM
lessons.summary: Design the software inside a cash machine with the State pattern, and get the money right when things fail halfway, such as when the account is debited but the notes jam, or the bank does not answer.

lessons.title: Vending machine
lessons.summary: Design a coin-operated snack machine with the State pattern, make correct change from a limited coin box, refund safely when an item gets stuck, and handle remote price changes and app reservations that arrive mid-sale.

lessons.title: Library management system
lessons.summary: Design a library system with books and physical copies, loans with due dates, a first-come-first-served reservation queue with pickup deadlines, overdue fines, and safe handling of two counters competing for the last copy.

lessons.title: Movie ticket booking
lessons.summary: Design the object model for booking cinema seats — temporary seat holds that expire, all-or-nothing reservations, and correct behaviour when two people click the same seat at the same moment.

lessons.title: Chess
lessons.summary: Model a chess game whose move validation covers every piece and correctly refuses any move that leaves your own king in check, with checkmate and stalemate detection built on top.

lessons.title: Snake and ladder
lessons.summary: Design a snakes-and-ladders game with a validated board, swappable house rules, deterministic dice for tests, and a clear game lifecycle, then compute the expected game length exactly.

lessons.title: Tic-tac-toe
lessons.summary: Design an N×N tic-tac-toe game with clean move validation, a fast win check, undo, and pluggable human or computer players, ending with an unbeatable minimax bot.

lessons.title: Card games
lessons.summary: Build a reusable card-game core (cards, deck, shuffling, hands) and a complete blackjack round on top of it, with a rule table for settlement, swappable dealer policies, and deterministic tests from stacked decks.

lessons.title: Food ordering
lessons.summary: Design the cart, bill and order lifecycle of a food ordering app — single-restaurant carts, a pluggable bill made of charge rules, a table-driven order state machine, and idempotent checkout.

lessons.title: Hotel booking
lessons.summary: Design availability search, short payment holds, confirmation, cancellation penalties and check-in for a hotel — with a half-open date range value object, decorated nightly rates and per-night inventory that can never double-book.

lessons.title: Payment gateway abstraction
lessons.summary: Hide several payment providers behind one interface — money in minor units, adapters that translate each provider's statuses and errors, routing with safe failover, a payment state machine, idempotent create and refund, and verified, de-duplicated webhooks.

lessons.title: Notification dispatcher
lessons.summary: Design the in-process engine that turns "notify user X" into a delivered SMS, push or email — channel plans with fallback, a filter chain for opt-outs, quiet hours and frequency caps, templates, priority lanes so OTPs never wait behind a marketing blast, and retries with backoff and jitter.

lessons.title: Logging framework
lessons.summary: Design a small structured-logging library — severity levels with per-category overrides, message templates that keep properties, enrichers and scopes, pluggable sinks and formatters, a bounded asynchronous sink with explicit drop policies, and an adapter so ASP.NET Core's ILogger writes through it.

lessons.title: Rate limiter (in-process)
lessons.summary: Design and build a thread-safe, in-process rate limiter in C# with token bucket, fixed window and sliding window algorithms, a testable clock (TimeProvider), per-key state with idle eviction, and an ASP.NET Core endpoint filter.

lessons.title: File system abstraction
lessons.summary: Design an in-memory virtual file system for a project document vault — a Composite tree of files and folders, a safe path value object, inherited ACL permissions with deny-wins, check-out locks, and content stored in a blob store without holding locks across I/O.

lessons.title: Inventory reservation
lessons.summary: Design a stock reservation engine that places time-limited holds during checkout, confirms or releases them, expires abandoned holds, never oversells under concurrency, and turns retried requests into safe replays with idempotency keys.

lessons.title: Order processing
lessons.summary: Design the order lifecycle of an online store — a table-driven state machine, an aggregate that raises domain events, authorise-then-capture payments with idempotency keys, optimistic concurrency, and a transactional outbox that triggers side effects reliably.

lessons.title: Employee leave and approval workflow
lessons.summary: Design a leave management module with working-day counting per office calendar (including the sandwich rule), reserved and used balances, a Chain of Responsibility that routes requests to the right approvers by authority, and State classes that make illegal moves impossible.

modules.title: Interview and Architecture Review
modules.description: Communicate, defend and review designs.

lessons.title: How system design interviews work
lessons.summary: Understand the formats of system design interviews, how to spend 45 or 60 minutes, what interviewers actually score, how LLD and HLD rounds differ, and the failure patterns that sink otherwise strong candidates.

lessons.title: Asking good clarifying questions and stating assumptions
lessons.summary: Ask the few questions that actually change the design, state assumptions with numbers when the interviewer leaves it to you, and turn the answers into a short list of functional requirements, measurable non-functional targets and an out-of-scope list.

lessons.title: Estimation practice drills
lessons.summary: Fourteen timed back-of-the-envelope drills with full arithmetic, the rounding tricks that make them fast, and a small C# drill generator and grader so you can practise until a five-minute estimate feels routine.

lessons.title: Defending database and messaging choices
lessons.summary: Learn the five-part sentence that defends any technology choice, build weighted decision matrices for databases and message brokers, practise four realistic push-back dialogues, and implement a small C# decision-matrix service that flags close calls and the criteria that decided them.

lessons.title: Recognising overengineering in interviews
lessons.summary: Learn to size a design to its requirements, spot the usual overengineering moves (and the underengineering ones), separate decisions that are cheap now and expensive later from those that can wait, and answer "what if it grows 100x?" with an evolution path instead of a bigger diagram.

lessons.title: Reviewing another engineer's design
lessons.summary: A repeatable way to review a design: read requirements first, walk the critical flows, kill a box, then run seven checklists (requirements, scale, failure, security, data, operations, cost). Learn to write feedback that is specific, ranked and kind, follow a complete worked review of a contractor-billing system, and build a C# review tool that ranks comments and lints feedback tone.

lessons.title: Handling changing requirements and migrations
lessons.summary: When the interviewer changes a requirement mid-design, use the five Rs (restate, re-estimate, ripple, revise, route) to adapt calmly, then show how the running system would migrate: expand and contract for schemas, dual writes with backfill and shadow reads for data stores, and gated cutovers with rollback. Includes a C# migration state machine and a resumable, idempotent backfill.

lessons.title: Mock interviews with rubrics
lessons.summary: Four complete, timed mock system design sessions (bus ticket booking, a live fantasy-cricket leaderboard, a site-photo and drone-imagery platform, and a marketplace payout system), each with the prompt card, hidden details for the interviewer, a minute-by-minute follow-up script, a model answer outline and a 1-4 rubric per dimension. Plus how to run mocks well and a C# scorecard and calibration tool.

modules.title: Capstone Projects and Graduation
modules.description: Three substantial projects that prove mastery.

lessons.title: Capstone A — Enterprise modular monolith
lessons.summary: Build and document a production-grade project and contract management system as a modular monolith on ASP.NET Core and PostgreSQL, with real authentication, resource-based authorization, validation, background processing and a full test suite, then defend it like a design review.

lessons.title: Capstone B — Distributed order processing
lessons.summary: Build an order pipeline split across several services that talk through RabbitMQ, with Redis-backed idempotency, an orchestrated saga with compensation, retries with backoff and jitter, dead-letter queues and a written failure analysis, and prove it survives crashes, duplicates and outages.

lessons.title: Capstone C — Production-style communication platform
lessons.summary: Build and operate a learning and communication platform with real-time course chat, asynchronous assignment workflows, search, multi-level caching, end-to-end observability with SLOs, Docker images and deployment documentation, and show that you can run it, not just write it.
